cells.tense: You're here, with the pen, and you've already thought your way to the floor of yourself.
cells.verb: following your own pattern down until thinking itself runs out
cells.place: in the place where who you are gets to show without dimming
cells.ask: if you like, sit with one person and let what you understand about yourself stay unsaid between you — just feel it recognized, yours and theirs both intact — so the depth keeps setting you free instead of standing alone.
cells.core: You've thought your way to the floor of who you are, and you've found the place where thinking stops. You're not stuck there; you're standing in it, and it fits. What you are doesn't need defending or explaining anymore — it just shows. That's rare, and it's quiet. What this is free to feed next is company: sitting beside someone with what you know, not to prove it, just to let it be felt alongside them, each of you whole.
cells.sheetLine: You've gone as deep as thought goes into yourself, and you're at home there.

cells.tense: You're living in a future where you've finally figured yourself out, and you keep not arriving.
cells.verb: digging further into your own pattern than the pattern goes
cells.place: in the place where who you are is supposed to simply show
cells.ask: say one plain thing about who you are, out loud to someone, as settled — before you've finished working it out — and let the shape of it hold on its own, so the depth starts freeing you instead of swallowing you.
cells.core: You're thinking about who you are harder than it can be thought. Every layer opens another layer, and somewhere ahead is the version where it all finally resolves — so you keep going down instead of showing up. The understanding was supposed to let you be yourself; instead it's become the thing standing between you and being yourself. What's missing isn't more depth. It's a plain statement you're willing to stand behind.
cells.sheetLine: You're trying to finish understanding yourself before you'll let yourself be seen.

cells.tense: You're standing at the edge of your own deep end, facing a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: staying in the shallows of your own pattern
cells.place: in the place where who you are is meant to come fully forward
cells.ask: join one shared thing this week — a table, a song, a gathering — and let yourself be glad in it with other people, without explaining yourself, and let that gladness pull you back toward understanding that frees.
cells.core: You're not going deep into who you are. The depth is there and you're keeping to the surface of it — a workable version of yourself that gets you through. It does get you through. But the real pattern of you is down there, unvisited, and the surface version is a little smaller than you are. The way back isn't to force yourself to think it through; it's to be among people, glad, belonging without having to match them — and the depth comes back on its own.
cells.sheetLine: You're living a smaller version of yourself than you actually understand.

cells.tense: You're already deep in yourself, pen down, calling it nothing.
cells.verb: understanding your own pattern further than you'll admit
cells.place: in the place where who you are is already showing
cells.ask: sit quietly with one thing you already know to be true about yourself, without arguing with it or passing it off, and let it be simply felt — so the depth you've reached gets to free you instead of running unclaimed.
cells.core: You already understand yourself more than you let on. People can feel it — the way you move, what you don't bother pretending about. But you call it overthinking, or coincidence, or you say you have no idea who you are. The depth is real and it's yours; you just haven't signed it. The way back is smaller than it sounds: not more thinking, but sitting still with what you already know and letting it be true.
cells.sheetLine: You know who you are better than you've said. The knowing is running; the owning isn't.

flags.detail: "a while ago" — a cell knows no one's past
